items.title: Red light: stop at the line
items.simple: A red light means stop. Stop at the white stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk or before you enter the intersection. Stay stopped while it is red, unless a turn is allowed.
items.official: At a red light, come to a complete stop at the stop line or, if there is no stop line, before entering the intersection or before reaching the crosswalk. Remain stopped as long as the signal is red, unless turns are allowed. Traffic signals apply to drivers, motorcycle riders, bicyclists, moped-riders and pedestrians.
items.mnemonic: Red: stop at the line and stay there.

items.title: Right turn on red
items.simple: You may turn right on red. First, stop all the way. Look both ways. Let people walking and other traffic go first. If you see a No Turn on Red sign or a red right arrow, wait for green.
items.official: You may turn right while the traffic signal displays a red light. Before turning, you must come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and other traffic. You may not turn right on red if signs are posted that read "No Turn on Red," or if a red arrow pointing to the right is displayed. Be sure to check for less visible vehicles such as motorcycles, bicycles and mopeds.
items.mnemonic: Right on red: stop, look, yield, then turn.

items.title: Left on red: one-way only
items.simple: You may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Stop completely, look both ways and let others go first. If you see a No Turn on Red sign or a red left arrow, wait.
items.official: You may turn left at a red light if you are on a one-way street and turning left onto another one-way street. Before turning, you must come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and other traffic. You may not turn left on red if signs read "No Turn on Red," or if a red arrow pointing to the left is displayed. Be sure to check for less visible vehicles such as motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds.
items.mnemonic: Left on red: one-way into one-way.

items.title: Red arrow: no turn
items.simple: A red arrow means stop if you want to go that way. In Virginia, you may not turn on a red arrow. A sign that says "Right or Left on Red Arrow After Stop" is one exception.
items.official: A red arrow means you must stop if you intend to move in the direction of the arrow. You may not proceed in the direction of the arrow as long as the red arrow is displayed, unless signs are posted that read "Right on Red Arrow After Stop" or "Left on Red Arrow After Stop." Virginia law prohibits right and left turns at red arrow lights.
items.mnemonic: Red arrow: no turn, unless a sign says so.

items.title: Flashing red: stop, then go
items.simple: A flashing red light means stop all the way. Let oncoming cars and people walking go first. Go when the way is clear. At a railroad crossing, stop even if you see no train.
items.official: At a flashing red light, come to a complete stop and yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. You may go when the way is clear. At a railroad crossing, you must come to a complete stop even if you don't see a train.

items.title: Flashing red arrow
items.simple: A flashing red arrow means stop all the way first. Let oncoming cars and people in the intersection go. Then, when the way is clear, you may turn in the direction the arrow points.
items.official: At a flashing red arrow, come to a complete stop, yield the right-of-way to vehicles coming from the other direction and pedestrians in the intersection, and proceed in the direction of the arrow when the way is clear.
items.mnemonic: Flashing red arrow: stop, look, then turn.

items.title: Yellow: about to change
items.simple: A yellow light or arrow means the light is about to change. If you have not entered the intersection and can stop safely, then stop. Otherwise, go through with care. Never speed up to beat the light.
items.official: A yellow light or arrow are cautions warning that the light is about to change. If you have not entered the intersection, stop; or, if unsafe to stop, cautiously go through it. If you are already in the intersection, go through it cautiously. Do not speed up to beat the light.
items.mnemonic: Yellow: stop if you safely can. Never race it.

items.title: Flashing yellow: slow down
items.simple: A flashing yellow light means slow down and go with care. You see these lights in places that are more dangerous than normal.
items.official: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Flashing yellow lights are at locations with higher-than-normal hazardous conditions.

items.title: Flashing yellow arrow: yield
items.simple: A flashing yellow arrow means you may turn that way if the way is clear. You do not go first. Let oncoming cars and people walking go first. Watch for motorcycles, bikes and mopeds.
items.official: At a flashing yellow arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow, if the way is clear. Yield the right-of-way to vehicles coming from the other direction and pedestrians in the intersection. Be sure to check for less visible vehicles such as motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds.

items.title: Green light: go if clear
items.simple: A green light means you may go if the way is clear. If you turn without a green arrow, let oncoming cars and people walking go first. Watch for motorcycles, bikes and mopeds.
items.official: At a green light, you may go if the way is clear. If you are turning without a green arrow, you must yield the right-of-way to vehicles coming from the other direction and pedestrians in the intersection. Be sure to check for less visible vehicles such as motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds.

items.title: Green arrow: go that way
items.simple: A green arrow means you may go the way it points. Make sure the way is clear first.
items.official: At a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if the way is clear.

items.title: Walker still in street
items.simple: Your red light just changed to green or to a flashing yellow arrow. A person is still walking in the street. Let that person finish crossing before you turn.
items.official: If a traffic light changes from red to green while a pedestrian is in the street, allow the pedestrian to cross the street before turning. If a traffic light changes from red to flashing yellow arrow while a pedestrian is in the intersection, allow the pedestrian to cross the street before turning.

items.title: Dark signal: all-way stop
items.simple: The traffic lights are not working and show no lights. Treat the intersection like an all-way stop. Stop, then take turns. If an officer is directing traffic or portable stop signs are up, follow them instead.
items.official: When traffic signals are not working because of a power outage or other problem and not displaying any lights, you are required to stop, proceeding through the intersection as though it were an all-way stop. This does not apply if a law enforcement officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, or if portable stop signs are in use.
items.mnemonic: Lights dark? Act like an all-way stop.

items.title: Officer beats the signal
items.simple: Always obey signs and signals. But if a police officer is directing traffic, do what the officer says. Never cut through a parking lot or field to get around a light or sign. That is against the law.
items.official: It is illegal to avoid these traffic controls by cutting through a parking lot or field. Obey all signs and signals unless directed by a police officer; always follow the officer's direction.
items.mnemonic: The officer outranks the light.

items.title: Red X: never this lane
items.simple: Lane use signals hang over lanes. They show which lanes you can use at different times of day. A red X over a lane means you must never drive in that lane.
items.official: Lane use signals indicate lanes where you can and cannot drive during different hours of the day. Red X: Never drive in a lane marked with a red X signal.
items.mnemonic: Red X = never. Yellow X = leave. Green arrow = drive.

items.title: Yellow X: leave the lane
items.simple: A yellow X over your lane means you should leave that lane. A yellow arrow pointing down at a slant means the same thing. Move to another lane as soon as it is safe.
items.official: Yellow X or Yellow Diagonal Downward Arrow: These signals mean that you should move out of the lane as soon as safely possible.
items.mnemonic: Red X = never. Yellow X = leave. Green arrow = drive.

items.title: Green lane arrow: drive here
items.simple: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may drive in that lane.
items.official: Green Arrow: You are permitted to drive in a lane marked with a green arrow signal.
items.mnemonic: Red X = never. Yellow X = leave. Green arrow = drive.

items.title: Left-turn arrow lane: turn only
items.simple: A white left-turn arrow over a lane can point one way or two ways. Enter that lane only to turn the way the arrow points. Do not use it to drive straight.
items.official: Left-turn Arrow: You are permitted to enter in a lane marked with a one-way or two-way arrow only to turn in the direction of the arrow.

items.title: Pedestrian hybrid beacon steps
items.simple: A pedestrian hybrid beacon warns you about people at a crosswalk. Solid yellow means get ready to stop. Two solid red lights mean stop. When the red lights flash back and forth, go with care if the crosswalk is clear.
items.official: PHBs appear over intersections without stoplights and alert drivers when pedestrians are at a crosswalk. One yellow light at the bottom flashes when a pedestrian activates the PHB. Next, the yellow light turns solid to alert drivers to prepare to stop. Then, the top two red lights turn solid while a walk signal appears, and drivers must stop. Lastly, the two red lights alternate flashing, telling the driver that if the crosswalk is now clear, they may proceed with caution.
items.mnemonic: Yellow: get ready. Solid red: stop. Flashing red: go if clear.

items.title: Red reflectors: wrong way
items.simple: Red reflectors on the road mark areas you must not enter. Only drivers going the wrong way can see them.
items.official: Red markings are generally not used. Red reflectors on the pavement show areas not to be entered or used. They are positioned on the road surface so that only traffic flowing in the wrong direction would observe them.
items.mnemonic: Red reflectors facing you? You're going the wrong way.

items.title: Broken yellow: may pass
items.simple: Yellow center lines mean traffic goes both ways. A broken yellow center line means you may pass on the left. Drivers going either way may pass. The way ahead must be clear.
items.official: Yellow center lines mean two-way traffic, flowing in opposite directions. Broken yellow center lines mean that passing on the left is allowed in either direction when the way ahead is clear.
items.mnemonic: Yellow = two-way. Broken = pass when clear.

items.title: Solid plus broken yellow
items.simple: With broken and solid yellow lines side by side, you may pass if the broken line is on your side. Otherwise, do not pass cars. You may cross the solid line only to pass walkers, bikes, scooters or skateboards safely.
items.official: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means that passing is allowed from the side of the broken line, but not from the side of the solid line. Vehicles on the solid yellow line side may only cross the line to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, and riders of scooters or skateboards, when the opposite lane is clear and you can pass safely.
items.mnemonic: Broken on your side? Pass. Solid on your side? Stay.

items.title: Double yellow: no passing
items.simple: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing either way. You may cross them only to turn left or to pass walkers, bikes, scooters or skateboards. The other lane must be clear, and the pass must be safe.
items.official: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of the road and separate traffic traveling in two different directions. Passing is not allowed in either direction. You may not cross the lines unless you are making a left turn or passing pedestrians, bicyclists, and riders of scooters or skateboards, when the opposite lane is clear and you can pass safely.
items.mnemonic: Double yellow = a wall. Cross only to turn left.

items.title: Broken white: change with care
items.simple: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same way. You may change lanes, but do it with care.
items.official: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic going in the same direction. You may change lanes with caution.
items.mnemonic: White = same way. Broken = may change.

items.title: Dotted white: stay in lane
items.simple: Dotted white lines are short white blocks set close together. They guide you through intersections so you stay in your lane. They also show where a turn lane, entrance lane or exit lane begins.
items.official: Dotted white lines are small rectangles closely spaced. They show lane assignment in intersections and interchanges where there might be a tendency to drift out of a lane. Often they guide two turning lanes through the intersection. They also denote the opening of a turn lane at an intersection and entrance/exit lanes at interchanges.

items.title: Unmarked two-lane road passing
items.simple: Many two-lane roads in Virginia have no lane lines. On these roads, you may pass a slow vehicle on the left. First, make sure no sign bans passing. Also make sure the way ahead is clear.
items.official: Many two-lane roads in Virginia do not have lane markings to separate the lanes. On an unmarked two-lane road, you may pass a slow moving vehicle on the left side if there are no signs prohibiting passing. Make sure that the way is clear.

items.title: Yield line of triangles
items.simple: A yield line is a row of white triangles across the lane. It shows where to yield, or stop if needed. You often see one where you enter a roundabout.
items.official: Yield line is a line of triangles extending across the roadway that may be used with a yield sign to show the point at which you must yield or stop, if necessary. A yield line is often seen at the entrance of a roundabout.
items.mnemonic: Triangle sign, triangle line: both mean yield.

items.title: Center turn lane: 150 feet
items.simple: On a three-lane road, broken yellow lines on both sides of the center lane let either direction pass. A solid and a broken yellow line on each side mean left turns only. Drive no more than 150 feet in it.
items.official: If the center lane is marked by a single broken yellow line on both sides, drivers traveling in either direction may use the center lane for passing. If both sides of the center lane are marked by a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, drivers traveling in either direction may use the lane for making left turns. However, they may not travel further than 150 feet in this lane.
items.mnemonic: Center turn lane: in, turn, out within 150 feet.

items.title: Sharrow: share with bikes
items.simple: A sharrow is a bike symbol painted in a lane, with two arrowheads above it. The lane is too narrow for a car and a bike to ride side by side. Expect bicyclists in that lane.
items.official: A shared lane marking, or sharrow, consists of a bicycle symbol with a double chevron arrow above it and is used on travel lanes too narrow for motor vehicles and bicycles to share side-by-side. Sharrows clarify where bicyclists are encouraged to ride in the lane and remind drivers to expect bicyclists on the road.
items.mnemonic: Sharrow = share + arrow. Share the lane with bikes.

items.title: Bike lane: turning only
items.simple: A bike lane has a bike symbol. It also has a solid or dashed white line, or green paint. Stay out of it unless you are turning. Before you turn, check your mirrors and yield to bikes.
items.official: Bicycle lanes are indicated by a solid or dashed white line or green pavement markings, and a bicyclist symbol. Drivers should not drive in the bicycle lane except when necessary to turn left or right. Before turning, check your mirrors for bicyclists that may be behind you and yield to bicycles in the lane.

items.title: Solid white: stay put
items.simple: Solid white lines show turn lanes. They tell you to avoid changing lanes near intersections, ramps and other risky spots. A solid white line also marks the road's right edge. Stop lines, crosswalks and parking spaces are white.
items.official: Solid white lines show turn lanes and discourage lane changes near intersections, interchange on- and off-ramps, and at other locations where lane changes might be dangerous. Solid white lines also mark the right edge of pavement. Stop lines, crosswalks and parking spaces also are marked by white lines.
items.mnemonic: White solid = stay put. White broken = may change.

items.title: White lane arrows
items.simple: White arrows are painted in lanes. A curved arrow means you must turn that way. A curved arrow with the word ONLY means the same. A curved arrow and a straight arrow together mean you may turn or go straight.
items.official: White lane arrows are curved or straight. If you are in a lane marked with a curved arrow or a curved arrow and the word ONLY, you must turn in the direction of the arrow. If your lane is marked with both a curved and straight arrow, you may turn or go straight.
items.mnemonic: Curved arrow alone: must turn. Plus straight: your choice.

items.title: Wrong-way arrows: pull over
items.simple: Big white arrows in the lane show the way traffic flows. If you are driving against the arrows, you are going the wrong way. You could crash head-on. Slow down and pull over right away.
items.official: Wrong-way arrows indicate that traffic only moves in the direction indicated by the arrow. If you drive against the direction of these arrows, you are going in the wrong direction and could get into a head-on crash. Immediately slow down and pull over.
items.mnemonic: Arrows pointing at you? Slow down and pull over.

items.title: Double white: do not cross
items.simple: Double solid white lines separate lanes going the same way. They often set apart a special lane, like an HOV lane. Never cross them. Enter the special lane only where signs and markings allow.
items.official: Double solid white lines separate lanes of traffic going in the same direction. Most often they are used to designate a special use lane from conventional lanes, such as High Occupancy Vehicle lanes. You may not cross these lines. You may enter the designated special use lane only where signs and markings allow.
items.mnemonic: Double white = a wall. Enter only where signs allow.

items.title: Bike box: stop behind it
items.simple: A bike box is a painted box, often green, with a bike symbol. At red lights, stop behind the box, not in it. Do not turn right on red there. When turning right on green, signal and yield to bikes.
items.official: Drivers must stop for a red traffic signal behind all bicycle boxes, not inside the box. Bicycle riders will move into the box in front of drivers at the intersection. Right turns on red are not allowed at these intersections. If turning right on a green light, drivers must signal and yield to bicycles on the right.
items.mnemonic: Bike box: bikes in front, you behind, no right on red.

items.title: Bus-only lanes
items.simple: Lanes marked BUS ONLY, or lanes with red pavement, are for buses.
items.official: Bus-only lanes are indicated by BUS ONLY markings and/or red-colored pavement.

items.title: Diamond marks HOV lane
items.simple: A white diamond in the lane marks an HOV lane. In heavy traffic, it is for buses, vanpools, carpools, motorcycles and some clean fuel cars. Signs show how many people you need and when the rule applies.
items.official: HOV lanes are marked by a diamond shape in the center of the lane. They may also be separated by a barrier or solid double white lines. During heavy traffic periods, HOV lanes are reserved for buses, vanpools, carpools, other high occupancy vehicles, motorcycles, and certain clean special fuel vehicles. Road signs show the minimum number of passengers and the times restrictions are in effect. Barrier-separated lanes are reversible. A diamond may also indicate a bus lane.
items.mnemonic: Diamond lane = more people in the car.

items.title: Toll plazas and E-ZPass
items.simple: Slow down at toll plazas. With E-ZPass, follow the purple E-ZPass signs. Without E-ZPass, use the cash-only lanes. If you enter an E-ZPass-only lane by mistake, do not stop. A camera photographs your plate, and the owner is billed.
items.official: All toll facilities in Virginia accept E-ZPass. If you have a transponder, follow signs with the purple E-ZPass logo; if not, follow signs for cash only lanes. Slow down as you approach toll plazas. If you enter an E-ZPass-only lane by mistake, do not stop. Stopping is unsafe and could cause a rear-end crash. Cameras will photograph the license plate and the registered owner will be billed.
items.mnemonic: Wrong toll lane? Don't stop. The camera handles it.

items.title: Painted curb colors
items.simple: Painted curbs have special rules. At white curbs, stop only to pick up or drop off people. At yellow curbs, stop only to load or unload, and stay with your car. At red curbs, do not stop, stand or park.
items.official: A painted curb means that you must follow special rules to park there. Check with the locality for specific meanings. Generally: White - Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers. Yellow - Stop only long enough to load or unload. Stay with your car. Red - Do not stop, stand or park. Some communities use red curbs to indicate no parking zones.
items.mnemonic: White = people. Yellow = load. Red = no stopping.

questions.explain: Drivers must stop behind a bicycle box at a red light, not inside the box.

questions.prompt: At an intersection with a bicycle box, what is the rule about right turns on red?
choices: They are allowed after a full stop
They are allowed only if no bicyclists are present
They are allowed only at night
questions.explain: Right turns on red are not allowed at intersections with bicycle boxes.

questions.prompt: What must you do when turning right on a green light at an intersection with a bike box?
choices: Signal and yield to bicycles on the right
Speed up to get ahead of the bicycles
Turn from inside the bike box
questions.explain: If you turn right on green at a bike box, you must signal and yield to bicycles on the right.

questions.prompt: This red lane is marked BUS ONLY. What kind of lane is it?
questions.explain: A lane marked BUS ONLY or with red pavement is reserved for buses.

questions.prompt: Besides BUS ONLY markings, what else may show that a lane is bus-only?
questions.explain: Bus-only lanes are shown by BUS ONLY markings or red-colored pavement.

questions.prompt: What does a diamond shape in the center of a lane show?
questions.explain: A diamond shape in the center of a lane marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane.

questions.prompt: HOV lanes separated by a barrier are reversible. What does reversible mean?
choices: You may drive in either direction at any time
Traffic flows one way at some times of day and the opposite way at other times
questions.explain: Barrier-separated HOV lanes are reversible. Traffic flows one way at certain times of day and the opposite way at other times.

questions.prompt: Where do you find the minimum number of passengers needed to use an HOV lane?
choices: Nowhere, because it is always the same
questions.explain: Road signs show the minimum number of passengers and the times when the HOV restrictions are in effect.

questions.prompt: During heavy traffic, HOV lanes are reserved for which vehicles?
questions.explain: During heavy traffic, HOV lanes are reserved for buses, vanpools, carpools, motorcycles and other high occupancy vehicles.

questions.prompt: Besides an HOV lane, what else may a diamond-shaped marking in a lane show?
questions.explain: A diamond-shaped marking may also show that a lane is reserved for buses.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you enter an E-ZPass-only high-speed lane by mistake?
choices: Stop and wait for a toll worker
Do not stop, and let the vehicle owner be billed for the toll
questions.explain: Do not stop, because stopping could cause a rear-end crash. The registered owner will be billed.

questions.prompt: You do not have an E-ZPass transponder. What should you do as you approach a toll plaza?
choices: Follow signs for cash only lanes
questions.explain: Without a transponder, you should look for and follow the signs for cash only lanes.

questions.prompt: What should you do as you approach, enter and leave a toll plaza?
choices: Slow down and be extra cautious, because toll employees may be crossing
questions.explain: Slow down and be extra cautious at toll plazas. Drivers may change lanes, and toll employees may cross.

questions.prompt: Some toll roads have high-speed lanes reserved for E-ZPass. What should you do if you do not have a transponder?
choices: Use those lanes and pay later
Stop in those lanes and pay cash
Use those lanes only at night
questions.explain: Those lanes are reserved for E-ZPass. Without a transponder, you should not enter them.

questions.prompt: What does a curb painted red mean?
choices: You may stop only to load or unload
You may stop only to pick up passengers
You may not stop, stand or park
You may park only at night
questions.explain: A red curb means that you must not stop, stand or park.

questions.prompt: What does a curb painted yellow generally mean?
choices: You may not stop at all
You may stop only to pick up or drop off passengers
You may park at any time
You may stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car
questions.explain: A yellow curb means you may stop only long enough to load or unload. You must stay with your car.

questions.prompt: What does a curb painted white generally mean?
choices: You may not stop, stand or park
You may stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers
You may stop only to load and unload freight
You may park there only if you are disabled
questions.explain: A white curb means you may stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers.
